titel: The end, as two friars remembered it
autor: Isambart de la Pierre and Martin Ladvenu, Dominicans of Rouen, before Guillaume Bouillé's inquiry
quelle: J. Quicherat (ed.), Procès de condamnation et de réhabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc, dite la Pucelle, vol. II (Paris: Renouard, 1844), pp. 4–9 (Préliminaires de la réhabilitation: Informatio prævia). Internet Archive, procsdecondam02joanuoft. Public domain.
hinweis: Eight excerpts read against the page images, in the French in which Quicherat prints the inquiry of 1450. The burning itself is not described here: where the friars describe it, the passage is cut and the cut marked [...]. The English is this site's working translation (CC0).

sections.blurb: The assessor who advised her to appeal to the council of Basel: Cauchon's 'be quiet, in the devil's name', her tears after the relapse, 'Farowelle', the missing secular sentence, and the cross he fetched from the nearest church.

units.orig: [...] dit et dépose qu'une fois, luy et plusieurs autres présens, on admonestoit et sollicitoit ladicte Jehanne de se submettre à l'Eglise. Sur quoy elle respondit, que voulontiers se submettoit au Saint Père, requérant estre menée à lui, et que point ne se submettroit au jugement de ses ennemis. Et, quant à ceste heure là, frère Isambert lui conseilla de se submettre au [général] concile de Basle, [et] ladicte Jeanne lui demanda que c'estoit que général concile. Respondit cellui qui parle, que c'estoit congrégacion de toute l'Eglise universelle et la chrestienté, et qu'en ce concile y en avoit autant de sa part, comme de la part des Anglois. Cela oy et entendu, elle commença à crier : « O ! puisqu'en ce lieu sont aucuns de nostre parti, je veuil bien me rendre et submettre au concile de Basle. » Et tout incontinent, par grant despit et indignacion, l'évesque de Beauvais commença à crier : « Taisez-vous, de par le dyable ! » et dist au notaire qu'il se gardast bien d'escrire la submission qu'elle avoit faicte au général concile de Basle. A raison de ces choses et plusieurs autres, les Anglois et leurs officiers menacèrent horriblement ledit frère Isambert, tellement que s'il ne se taisoit, le gecteroient en Seine.
units.en: [...] he says and testifies that once, when he and several others were present, Jeanne was being admonished and urged to submit to the Church. To which she answered that she willingly submitted to the Holy Father, asking to be taken to him, and that she would not submit to the judgement of her enemies. And at that moment brother Isambart advised her to submit to the [general] council of Basel, [and] Jeanne asked him what a general council was. The witness answered that it was the gathering of the whole universal Church and of Christendom, and that in that council there were as many of her side as of the English side. Having heard and understood this, she began to cry out: 'Oh! since there are some of our party in that place, I am quite willing to give myself up and submit to the council of Basel.' And at once, in great spite and indignation, the bishop of Beauvais began to shout: 'Be quiet, in the devil's name!' and told the notary to take good care not to write down the submission she had made to the general council of Basel. For these things and several others the English and their officers threatened brother Isambart horribly, so that if he did not keep quiet they would throw him into the Seine.
units.note: Isambart de la Pierre, assessor at the trial, sworn and examined on 5 March 1450 (1449 in the old reckoning, the year then beginning at Easter). The French text of 1450 calls him an Augustinian; the Latin depositions of 1452 call him a Dominican (Quicherat II, p. 348). The submission to the Church was the hinge of the case (Interr. Prison [1], Art. Twelve [3]); by Isambart's account an appeal to the pope and a submission to the council of Basel were made and kept out of the record. The council had opened in July 1431, after her death; it had been convoked before.

units.titel: 'Farowelle, faictes bonne chière, il est faict'
units.orig: Item dit et dépose que, après qu'elle eust renoncé et abjuré, et reprins habit d'homme, lui et plusieurs autres furent présens, quant ladicte Jehanne s'excusoit de ce qu'elle avoit revestu habit d'homme, en disant et affermant publiquement que les Anglois lui avoient faict ou faict faire en la prison beaucoup de tort et de violence, quant elle estoit vestue d'habits de femme ; et de fait, la veit éplourée, son viaire plain de larmes, deffiguré et oultraigié en telle sorte que celui qui parle en eut pitié et compassion. Item dit et rapporte que devant toute l'assistance, lorsqu'on la réputoit hérectique obstinée et rencheue, elle respondit publiquement : « Si vous, Messeigneurs de l'Eglise, m'eussiez menée et gardée en vos prisons, par advanture ne me fust-il pas ainsi. » Item dit et dépose que, après l'yssue et la fin de ceste session et instance, ledit seigneur évesque de Beauvais dist aux Anglois qui dehors attendoient : « Farowelle, faictes bonne chière, il est faict. »
units.en: He also says and testifies that after she had renounced and abjured, and taken men's clothes again, he and several others were present when Jeanne excused herself for having put on men's clothes again, saying and affirming publicly that the English had done her, or had had done to her, much wrong and violence in the prison when she was dressed in women's clothes; and indeed he saw her in tears, her face full of tears, disfigured and outraged, so that the witness had pity and compassion on her. He also says and reports that before the whole assembly, when she was held to be an obstinate and relapsed heretic, she answered publicly: 'If you, my lords of the Church, had taken me and kept me in your prisons, perhaps it would not be so with me.' He also says and testifies that after the end of this session the bishop of Beauvais said to the English who were waiting outside: 'Farewell, be of good cheer, it is done.'
units.note: 28 May 1431, the session of the relapse (Ouen Relapse [1]–[2]). 'Farowelle' is the English 'farewell' in French spelling; Quicherat notes that an earlier editor printed a form 'which is in no language'. The question of her prison, a lay prison in the castle guarded by English soldiers instead of a church prison, runs through both friars' depositions.

units.orig: Item dit et dépose avoir bien veu et clairement apperceu, à cause qu'il a tousjours esté présent, assistant à toute la déduction et conclusion du procez, que le juge séculier ne l'a poinct condamnée à mort, ne à consumpcion de feu ; et combien que le [dit] juge lay et séculier se soit comparu et trouvé au lieu même où elle fut preschée derrenièrement et délaissée à justice séculière, toutesfois, sans jugement ou conclusion dudit juge, a esté livrée entre les mains du bourreau et bruslée, en disant au bourreau tant seulement, sans autre sentence : « Fais ton devoir. »
units.en: He also says and testifies that he saw well and clearly perceived, since he was present throughout and attended the whole conduct and conclusion of the trial, that the secular judge did not condemn her to death, nor to burning; and although the said lay and secular judge appeared and was present in the very place where she was last preached to and left to the secular arm, nevertheless, without judgement or decision of that judge, she was handed over to the executioner and burned, with no more said to the executioner, and no other sentence, than: 'Do your duty.'
units.note: The church court did not sentence anyone to death: it declared her a relapsed heretic and 'left' her to the secular arm (Ouen Sentence [1]). The secular court was then to pass sentence. Both friars say it never did. For the nullity trial this was a fault of procedure; for the reader it is the moment where the two jurisdictions each left the death to the other.

units.titel: The cross from the nearest church
units.orig: Item dépose celui qui parle, que ladicte Jehanne eut en la fin si grande contricion et si belle repentance, que c'estoit une chose admirable, en disant parolles si dévotes, piteuses et catholiques, que tous ceulx qui la regardoient, en grant multitude, pleuroient à chaudes larmes, tellement que le cardinal d'Angleterre et plusieurs autres Anglois furent contraincts plourer et en avoir compacion. Dit oultre plus, que la piteuse femme lui demanda, requist et supplia humblement, ainsi qu'il estoit près d'elle en sa fin, qu'il allast en l'église prouchaine, et qu'il lui apportast la croix, pour la tenir eslevée tout droit devant ses yeux jusques au pas de la mort, afin que la croix où Dieu pendist, fust en sa vie continuellement devant sa vue. Dit oultre, qu'elle [...] oncques ne cessa jusques en la fin de résonner et confesser à haulte voix le saint nom de Jhesus, en implorant et invocant sans cesse l'ayde des Saincts et Sainctes de paradis ; et encores, qui plus est, en rendant son esperit et inclinant la teste, proféra le nom de Jhesus, en signe qu'elle estoit fervente en la foy de Dieu, ainsi comme nous lisons de saint Ignatius et plusieurs autres martyrs. [...]
units.en: The witness also testifies that at the end Jeanne showed such great contrition and so fine a repentance that it was a thing to wonder at, saying words so devout, so moving and so catholic that all who watched her, in a great multitude, wept hot tears, so that the cardinal of England and several other Englishmen were forced to weep and to feel compassion. He says further that the poor woman asked, begged and humbly entreated him, as he was near her at the end, to go into the nearest church and bring her the cross, to hold it upright before her eyes until the moment of death, so that the cross on which God hung might be before her sight continually while she lived. He says further that she [...] never ceased to the end to proclaim and confess aloud the holy name of Jesus, calling without ceasing on the help of the saints of paradise; and more than that, as she gave up her spirit and bowed her head, she spoke the name of Jesus, in sign that she was fervent in the faith of God, as we read of Saint Ignatius and many other martyrs. [...]
units.note: 30 May 1431, the Old Market at Rouen. The first cut leaves out four words placing her in the fire; the second, the end of the deposition, in which the executioner came to the two friars afterwards in despair, fearing he would never be forgiven, and told them what he had not been able to burn. Neither is carried here. The cardinal of England is Henry Beaufort, bishop of Winchester, great-uncle of Henry VI.

sections.blurb: Her confessor in the last days: the lay prison kept 'for fear of displeasing the English', what she told him of the violence done to her, 'I die through you', the case of Georges Folenfant, and the executioner's fear.

units.orig: [...] Principalement cellui qui parle, dit du couraige et de l'affeccion excessive de messire Pierre Cauchon, alors évesque de Beauvais, sur lui allégant deux signes d'envye : le premier, quant ledit évesque se portoit pour juge, commanda ladicte Jehanne estre gardée ès prisons séculières, et entre les mains de ses ennemis mortelz ; et quoy qu'il eust bien peu la faire détenir et garder aux prisons ecclésiastiques, toutesfois si a-t-il permis depuis le commencement du procez jusques à la consommacion, icelle tormenter et traictier très cruellement aux prisons séculières. Dit oultre davantaige ce tesmoing, qu'en la première session ou instance, l'évesque allégué requist et demanda le conseil de toute l'assistance, assavoir lequel estoit plus convenable de la garder et détenir aux prisons séculières, ou aux prisons de l'Eglise ; sur quoy fut délibéré, qu'il estoit plus décent de la garder aux prisons ecclésiastiques qu'aux autres ; fors, respondit cest évesque, qu'il n'en feroit pas cela, de paour de desplaire aux Anglois. Le second signe qu'il allègue, est que le jour que ledit évesque, avec plusieurs, la déclaira hérectique, récidivée et retournée à son meffait pour cela qu'elle avoit dedans la prison reprins habit d'homme, ledit évesque sortissant de la prison, advisa le conte de Warwick et grant multitude d'Anglois entour lui, auxquelz en riant dist à haulte voix intelligible : « Farowelle, Farowelle, il en est faict, faictes bonne chière, » ou parolles semblables.
units.en: [...] Above all the witness speaks of the disposition and excessive partiality of master Pierre Cauchon, then bishop of Beauvais, alleging two signs of ill will against him. The first: when the bishop set himself up as judge, he ordered Jeanne to be kept in the secular prisons, in the hands of her mortal enemies; and although he could well have had her held and kept in the church's prisons, he nevertheless allowed her, from the beginning of the trial to its end, to be tormented and treated very cruelly in the secular prisons. The witness says further that at the first session the bishop asked the advice of the whole assembly as to which was more fitting, to keep and hold her in the secular prisons or in the prisons of the Church; on which it was resolved that it was more decent to keep her in the church's prisons than in the others; but, the bishop answered, he would not do that, for fear of displeasing the English. The second sign he alleges is that on the day when the bishop, with several others, declared her a heretic, relapsed and returned to her misdeed because she had taken men's clothes again in prison, the bishop, coming out of the prison, saw the earl of Warwick and a great crowd of English round him, to whom he said laughing, in a loud and clear voice: 'Farewell, farewell, it is done, be of good cheer,' or words like these.
units.note: Martin Ladvenu, Dominican of Saint-Jacques at Rouen, 'special confessor and guide of Jeanne in her last days', examined on the same day, 5 March 1450. The two friars report Cauchon's 'Farowelle' in almost the same words; they belonged to the same convent and testified the same day. Richard Beauchamp, earl of Warwick, was governor of the young Henry VI; Quicherat calls him the principal agent of her death.

units.orig: Item dit et rapporte que, à la conscience, en lui proposoit et demandoit questions trop difficiles, pour la prendre à ses parolles et à son jugement ; car c'estoit une pouvre femme assez simple, qui à grant peine savoit Pater noster et Ave Maria. Item dépose que la simple Pucelle lui révéla, que, après son abjuracion et renonciacion, on l'avoit tourmentée violemment en la prison, molestée, bastue et deschoullée ; et qu'un millourt d'Angleterre l'avoit forcée ; et disoit publicquement que cela estoit la cause pourquoy elle avoit reprins habit d'homme : et environ la fin, dist à l'évesque de Beauvais : « Hélas ! je meurs par vous, car se m'eussiez baillée à garder ès prisons de l'Église, je ne fusse pas icy. »
units.en: He also says and reports that, to his knowledge, questions too difficult were put to her, to catch her in her words and her judgement; for she was a poor, rather simple woman, who hardly knew the Pater noster and the Ave Maria. He also testifies that the simple Maid told him that after her abjuration and renunciation she had been violently tormented in the prison, molested, beaten and dragged about; and that an English milord had forced her; and she said publicly that this was the reason why she had taken men's clothes again. And near the end she said to the bishop of Beauvais: 'Alas! I die through you, for if you had given me into the keeping of the Church's prisons, I would not be here.'
units.note: What she told her confessor, as he reported it nineteen years later; it is given here as he gave it. 'Forcer' in fifteenth-century French can mean to violate or to use force on. In 1456 the notary Manchon testified that she had complained to the bishop and to Warwick that her guards had several times tried to violate her, and that once Warwick came at her cries and stopped them (Quicherat III, pp. 147–148, not carried here). On the Pater noster: at her first session she offered to say the Pater noster to the bishop if he would hear her confession (Interr. Public [2]).

units.orig: Item dit et dépose que quant elle fut derrenierrement preschée au Viel-Marché, et abbandonnée à justice séculière, combien que les juges séculiers fussent assis sur un escherffault, toutesfois elle ne fut nullement condampnée d'aucun d'iceulx juges, mais sans condampnacion, par deux sergens fut contraincte de descendre de l'escherffault, et menée par lesditz sergens jusques au lieu où elle devoit estre bruslée, et par iceulx livrée entre les mains du bourreau. Et en signe de ce, peu de temps après, un appellé Georges Folenfant fut appréhendé à cause de la foy et en crime d'hérésie, lequel fut semblablement délaissé à justice séculière. A ceste cause, les juges de la foy, c'est assavoir, messire Loys de Luxembourg, archevesque de Rouen, et frère Guillaume Duval, vicaire de l'inquisiteur de la foy, envoyèrent ledit frère Martin au bailly de Rouen, pour l'advertir qu'il ne seroit pas ainsi faict dudit Georges comme il avoit été faict de la Pucelle, laquelle, sans sentence finale et jugement deffinitif, fut au feu consommée.
units.en: He also says and testifies that when she was last preached to in the Old Market and abandoned to the secular arm, although the secular judges were seated on a platform, she was not condemned by any of those judges at all; but without condemnation she was made to come down from the platform by two sergeants, and led by them to the place where she was to be burned, and handed by them to the executioner. And as a sign of this, a little later one Georges Folenfant was arrested on a matter of faith and for the crime of heresy, and was likewise left to the secular arm. For this reason the judges of the faith, namely master Louis of Luxembourg, archbishop of Rouen, and brother Guillaume Duval, vicar of the inquisitor of the faith, sent brother Martin to the bailli of Rouen, to warn him that it should not be done with Georges as it had been done with the Maid, who without final sentence or definitive judgement was put to death by fire.
units.note: The same point as Isambart's (End Isambart [3]), with a proof from the next case: the church judges themselves sent Ladvenu to make sure the secular court passed sentence the next time. Louis of Luxembourg, brother of Jean de Luxembourg who had sold her to the English (Mon. [4], note), became archbishop of Rouen only in 1436 and was chancellor of France for the English; Ladvenu's 'a little later' was some years.

units.orig: Item dit et dépose que le bourreau, après la combustion, quasi à quatre heures après nones, disoit que jamais n'avoit tant crainct à faire l'exécucion d'aucun criminel, comme il avoit eu la combustion de la Pucelle, pour plusieurs causes : premièrement, pour le grant bruit et renom d'icelle ; secondement, pour la cruelle manière de la lier et afficher [...] ; de quoy il estoit fort marry, et avoit grant compassion de la forme et cruelle manière par laquelle on la faisoit mourir. Item dépose de sa grant et admirable contricion, repentance et continuelle confession, en appellant tousjours le nom de Jhesus, et invocant dévotement l'ayde des Saincts et Sainctes de paradis, ainsi comme frère Isambert, qui tousjours l'avoit convoyée à son trespas et raddressée en la voye du salut, cy devant a déposé.
units.en: He also says and testifies that the executioner, after the burning, at about four in the afternoon, said that he had never been so afraid to carry out the execution of any criminal as he had been at the burning of the Maid, for several reasons: first, because of her great fame and renown; second, because of the cruel manner in which she was bound and set up [...]; at which he was much grieved, and had great compassion for the form and cruel manner in which she was put to death. He also testifies to her great and admirable contrition, repentance and continual confession, always calling on the name of Jesus and devoutly invoking the help of the saints of paradise, as brother Isambart, who had accompanied her to her death and kept her on the way of salvation, has testified above.
units.note: The cut gives the executioner's reason in his own terms, the height of the platform the English had built, which kept him from doing what he otherwise could; it is not carried here. The deposition ends where the man who carried out the sentence says he pitied the manner of it, and the confessor returns to her words.
